title: Record property verification as work only an operator can complete
statement: Establishing ownership of a site in a search platform's console is recorded as a task requiring a person with access to that account and to DNS or the origin, and is never reported as done on the basis of a repository change alone.
rationale: Verification depends on state inside an account this process cannot see, so treating a committed verification file as proof of a verified property records a result that may not exist.
implementation: Prepare whatever the chosen method needs, a DNS record value or a file at a fixed path, and hand it over as an instruction naming the account and the method. Record the outcome only once the operator reports it.

verification.method: Confirm with the operator that the property shows as verified in the console, and record which method and which account was used.

caution: A verification file present in the repository shows an intent to verify, not a verified property. The two are recorded separately because a deployment can drop the file without the console reflecting it immediately.

title: Announce a new sitemap through the platform's own submission route
statement: A sitemap that has just started being served is declared to each platform once, through that platform's console or its documented ping endpoint, in addition to being referenced from robots.txt.
rationale: A sitemap referenced only from robots.txt is found when the file is next fetched rather than when it changes, so a first publication can wait longer than the operator expects.
implementation: Submit the index rather than each child sitemap, and do it once at first publication rather than on every rebuild. Later changes are picked up from the file itself.

verification.method: Confirm the sitemap appears in each platform's submitted-sitemaps list and record the reported fetch status and date.

caution: Submission causes the file to be fetched; it does not determine which of its addresses are indexed, and no submission status here supports a claim about indexing.

title: Host the IndexNow key file where the protocol requires
statement: The key file is served as plain text at a location the protocol permits for the addresses being submitted, containing exactly the key used in submissions, and the submission names that location when it is not the site root.
rationale: A submission whose key cannot be fetched at a permitted location is rejected, so a key file behind a redirect, at the wrong path, or with a mismatched body makes every submission fail while appearing to have been sent.
implementation: Serve the key from the same configuration value the submitter reads, so rotating the key updates both at once. Confirm the edge does not answer the key path with a redirect or a challenge.

verification.method: Fetch the key location from the production host and compare the served body, status, and content type against the key the submitter sends.

title: Submit only addresses that are public and canonical
statement: Each submitted address returns a success status without credentials, is the canonical form of its page, and is not excluded from indexing by robots.txt or by a directive.
rationale: Submitting an address the platform is told not to index, or one that redirects elsewhere, spends the submission on a page that cannot be accepted and reports a private or superseded address to a third party.
implementation: Build the submission list from the same declared indexable inventory the sitemap uses, rather than from a change feed that reports every modified record including drafts.

verification.method: Request each address queued for submission without credentials and reject any that redirects, fails, or carries an exclusion directive before the batch is sent.

title: Isolate submission failures from page rendering
statement: A submission call runs outside the request that publishes the content, with a timeout and a bounded number of retries, so an unavailable or slow endpoint cannot delay or fail the publish itself.
rationale: A notification to a third party is the least important part of publishing, and code that awaits it inline makes the site's own availability depend on a service the site does not run.
implementation: Enqueue the submission and return from the publish path immediately, retrying from the queue with a ceiling and recording each attempt's outcome per address rather than per batch.

verification.method: Publish content with the submission endpoint made unreachable and confirm the publish completes normally while the failure is recorded for retry.

caution: That a dependency on an external service should not gate a local operation is an architectural property of the site, not a documented protocol rule, so it carries no external citation.

title: Read a submission acknowledgement as receipt rather than indexing
statement: A success response to a submission is recorded as evidence that the request was accepted, and no report derives from it a claim that any address was crawled, indexed, or shown to a reader.
rationale: The acknowledgement describes the fate of the request, not the fate of the page, and conflating the two produces a report claiming indexing that nothing observed.
implementation: Log the response status against the submitted address and label the record as a submission receipt. Read indexing state, where it is needed, from the platform's own reporting instead.

verification.method: Review submission logs and any report built from them, confirming no statement about crawling or indexing rests on a submission response alone.

caution: The protocol documents what the response codes mean and stops there, which is exactly the point: it makes no promise about indexing, so neither may any report built on it. Submission also does not replace serving a sitemap.
